preamble: FH has the same meaning throughout

clue.text: Bed lice make some noise

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bedbugs, or lice in the bed, are kicking up a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' signals the anagram of BEDLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is a unit measuring loudness, so it quantifies some amount of sound.

clue.text: Beetle having married insect is sleeping

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A beetle wed to another bug is fast asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive, as if asleep, like a resting volcano or seed.

clue.text: Funny fuel frames Rufus's final full year

indicators.note: one piece surrounds the other like a picture frame

parts.note: coal is a fuel
William II, called Rufus, died in August 1100, so his last whole year was 1099, here written loosely in Roman numerals as one before eleven hundred

explanation.surface: Fuel gives a frame to some red-haired person's last whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 1099 is MXCIX; MIC is a loose Roman shorthand (one subtracted from 1100) but the intended reading is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical means amusing, causing laughter, the same as funny.

clue.text: FH for 12 having died

definitions.note: facial hair, as the preamble defines it

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is a bear's name, standing for bear
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Facial hair taken from a dead bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is BRUIN, a name for a bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair growing on the chin and cheeks is the fullest form of growth on the face.

clue.text: Trenet's song about the heartless supermarket hasn't been here long

indicators.note: the song goes round the other piece

parts.note: La Mer is Charles Trenet's famous French song

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: Tesco is a big British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A French singer's song about a soulless superstore is a recent arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: La Mer is Charles Trenet's French song; Tesco is a big British supermarket chain. 'heartless' takes out the middle letter and 'about' wraps the song round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer is a newcomer who arrived recently, someone new to a place.

clue.text: FH for one making meringues, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in this puzzle FH stands for facial hair, and a single bristle of a moustache qualifies
a kitchen tool or person that beats egg whites stiff

explanation.surface: A bit of facial hair is offered as the thing that whips up meringues.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's FH means facial hair throughout the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue needs egg whites beaten stiff, the job of a hand beater; separately a single hair of a moustache is one too.

clue.text: The Guardian has a line that isn't fresh

parts.note: the newspaper's editorial voice speaks of itself as we
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A newspaper admits running something stale.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Guardian puzzle the paper itself is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weary is being tired, the opposite of rested and lively.

clue.text: Restrained at home and didn't show hurt inside

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: one piece sits within another

parts.note: hid means kept out of sight
a bite is a sting or hurt

explanation.surface: Someone stayed in and concealed their pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the hurt within the concealing word; 'at home' is a standard crossword sense of in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhibited means held back by self-consciousness, kept in check.

clue.text: He was beat and needed a cure all right

indicators.note: the letters were needed to be worked into a new form, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: A worn-out man needed treatment to be fine again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' means the Beat Generation, not exhausted; 'needed' rearranges A CURE with OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Kerouac wrote On the Road and was the leading novelist of the Beat Generation.

clue.text: Elevation of monarch about to join followers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means reading upwards, so backwards
the monarch's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
to unite is to join

explanation.surface: A king's rise draws attendants to his side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the joining word inside the Queen's cipher, and 'Elevation of' turns the whole thing up the column, as a down entry reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Defence gets beast to leave

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a beast of the field
to part is to depart or leave

explanation.surface: A defensive line is breached when a creature is allowed to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive earth wall around a fort, a fortification.

clue.text: A model for an artist needing a drink

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
Damien Hirst is a British artist known for the shark in formaldehyde

explanation.surface: An artist's sitter is gasping for refreshment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a sitter for the artist, but it is the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Athirst is an old adjective meaning thirsty, which is exactly wanting liquid refreshment.

clue.text: River out of churchyard meandering into Austria, perhaps

indicators.note: wandering about, so the remaining letters wander into a new order
the river's letter is taken out of the churchyard's letters

explanation.surface: A river leaves a churchyard and winds its way into Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes one R from CHURCHYARD, and 'meandering' rearranges CHUCHYARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria was ruled as an archduchy by the Habsburgs, a territory under an archduke, so it is an example.

clue.text: Name for beast makin' beer, do you hear?

indicators.note: asks the solver to listen, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: making beer is brewing, and the dropped g gives brewin'

explanation.surface: A homebrewer is asked what to call a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in makin' hints that brewing loses its g.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional folk name for the bear, from the bear in the Reynard tales.

clue.text: Ploughing with lean horse?

parts.note: to lean is to tilt
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether a skinny horse can pull the plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like an adjective for the horse but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is cultivation of the soil, the working of land by tillage.

clue.text: Winter ate away Scot and Irish

indicators.note: the named letters are taken away

parts.note: to winter is to hibernate
Ian is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: In winter a Scot and an Irishman ate everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winter' is a verb; 'away' removes 'ate' from it. Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is Latin for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish.

clue.text: FH of computer operator accepting informal chat

definitions.note: facial hair, as the preamble defines it

indicators.note: one thing takes another inside it

parts.note: a mouse is the device used to operate a computer

indicators.note: casual, out of formal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a keyboard has whiskers and enjoys a casual natter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informal' rearranges the chat, which 'accepting' places inside the device a computer user operates by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip is the classic example of a growth on the face.

clue.text: Great 12 using top of juggernaut as armour

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new order
the first letter of the word, as at the top of a down entry

explanation.surface: A huge bear uses the front of a lorry as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is BRUIN, so 'Great 12' is the Great Bear. 'top of' gives J; 'using' rearranges it with AS ARMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major is Latin for the Great Bear, the constellation.

clue.text: FH as conceit used by poet

definitions.note: facial hair, as the preamble defines it

parts.note: side is old slang for pretentiousness or swagger, conceit
Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: A poet uses facial hair as a literary conceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceit' looks like a literary figure but means swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown down the cheeks in front of the ears counts as growth on the face.

clue.text: Sun to depart, right, traditionally without 3

parts.note: Sol is Latin for the sun
to die is to depart this life

explanation.surface: The sun goes down, as is proper, on a clean-shaven man.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is BEARD; soldiers were traditionally made to shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies traditionally required troops to be clean-shaven, so a fighting man was one without a chin growth.

clue.text: Spirited gadabout swallowing bone

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: read as gad about, the word gad turned round
the shin is a bone of the leg

explanation.surface: A party-goer gulps down a bone with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gadabout' splits as 'gad about': the word gad turned about, which is 'swallowing' the leg bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing means lively and stylish, full of spirit and verve.

clue.text: Rich man goes down rapidly

definitions.meaning: Latin for rich, and the name given to the wealthy man in the parable of Lazarus

explanation.surface: A wealthy man takes a sudden plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable's rich man is traditionally named from the Latin for wealthy; and to plunge headfirst is to drop sharply.

clue.text: 3 painter consigns vehicle to ditch

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a dyke is a ditch or drain

explanation.surface: An artist dumps his van in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is BEARD: a Vandyke is a pointed beard named after the painter Anthony van Dyck. 'consigns ... to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Dyck, sometimes spelt so, was the Flemish portraitist whose sitters' pointed chin hair took his name.

clue.text: Fiddle encompassing solvers went wrong

indicators.note: surrounding another piece

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin
the solvers are addressed as you, old form ye

explanation.surface: A violin surrounded by puzzlers went off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like cheating; it is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off the right path, to go astray.

clue.text: In a cathedral a service requires concentration

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Attending a cathedral service demands focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside the run 'cathedral a service'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a tightly focused beam of light, light concentrated into a narrow stream.

clue.text: Nothing new devised in poet or — mortgage company?

indicators.note: one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: Homer is the Greek epic poet
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: made up or contrived, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Something new is invented in a poem, or perhaps it's a lender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges O and NEW to EOWN, which goes 'in' HOMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a mortgage keeps company with others who own property; the question mark flags the loose sense of borrowers as a group.

clue.text: Something of Christmas left among the sacred

indicators.note: one piece goes amid the other

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: A remnant of Christmas sits with sacred things.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen with red berries is a traditional seasonal decoration.

clue.text: Worked without leader so that all should go smoothly?

definitions.text: so that all should go smoothly?

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: toiled is another word for worked hard

explanation.surface: Laboured, headless, to keep things running easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' drops T from TOILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lubricated has had grease applied so parts run with less friction.

clue.text: Roman two with Latin twist to start with

indicators.note: a twist turns the letters into a new order

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Two Romans give their Latin a twist at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges II and LATIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something initial comes first, at the beginning, as a starting point does.

clue.text: Shaker near to Dickensian whose charity began abroad

parts.note: a jelly shakes and wobbles
by means beside or near

explanation.surface: A Shaker sits beside a Dickens character famous for overseas good works.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Jellyby in Bleak House neglects her family for an African mission, inverting 'charity begins at home'. 'Shaker' looks like the religious sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Jellyby is the Bleak House philanthropist devoted to distant causes over her household.

clue.text: Period of The Caretaker?

parts.note: The Caretaker reads like the Pinter play, but means a ruler minding the throne for a monarch, and the clue asks for that stretch of time

explanation.surface: A question about when Pinter's play is set.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caretaker is a Harold Pinter play; here it means a regent who holds power for an absent or young monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of a monarch, so the term of that rule is a caretaker's period.

clue.text: R for Rebekah

definitions.meaning: the letter R is the leading letter of the colour red
Rebekah Brooks, newspaper executive famous for her red hair

explanation.surface: A letter stands for a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebekah Brooks was the flame-haired News International chief executive in the 2011 phone-hacking scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: R begins the word red, so it is that colour's head; and a person with ginger hair is so called.
